title: `$uri->queryParameter($name)` parses the whole query string again on every call.
text: `nvs_core_uri_query_parameter` (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/uri.rs:2679`) runs `parse_query` over the receiver's query slot and drops the array after one lookup, so a program that reads each of P parameters off one `Core\Uri` costs O(P²). `Core\Request::query` holds its parse on the request; a `Uri` is an immutable instance of eight slots with nowhere to keep one. The two answers: a memo slot on the instance, which is per-instance memory of the query's size, or a stated bound whose card sends a program reading many names to `parseQuery()` once. Ladder: a `run` ladder that builds one `Uri` with P parameters and reads each once.
